newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-NYMEX crude may dip to $21 on profit takin.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-NYMEX crude may dip to $21 on profit takin.

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20
+ NYMEX crude oil may slip lower on profit taking towards $21 a barrel after recent sharp gains, technical analysts said.
+ Heating oil was weaker in overnight trading but had "unfinished business" to the upside, they said.
+ Gasoline is well support and should find good buying on any dip lower to 64 cents a gallon.
NYMEX crude oil futures may slip lower during pit trading on Tuesday due to profit taking after a storming rally that lifted prices 95 cents a barrel on Monday.
The June contract ended a cent below Monday's close at $21.37 a barrel on overnight ACCESS trading.
"The market has done what it has to do for the moment (on the upside)," said Charles Gray of Prudential Bache in London.
He saw support at in the range $20.97 to $21.02 and below that at $20.50.
Other brokers also saw a strong chance of weaker levels after recent strong gains but the speed of the rally has left few obvious support levels.
MeesPierson Derivatives in London saw support at $21.35, $21 and then $20.50.
Gray said heating oil "still has some unfinished business," and might head for 57.50 cents a gallon at a later date.
The June contract ended down 0.15 cent at 56.50 cents a gallon but should find support at 56.00.
MeesPierson saw the chance of scale down buying at 56.40, 56.00 and the 55.60 areas.
"Below this we would cut longs," they said in a market report.
Gasoline remains well supported technically. "Support and buying level is now 63.90/64.00," MeesPierson said.
The June contract ended up 0.53 cents at 65.00 cents a gallon on the overnight ACCESS trading system.
-- Sam Arnold-Forster, London Newsroom +44 171 542 4984
